worksheet.title: Who Is Ahead?
worksheet.subtitle: Run both, then compare the landings
worksheet.learning_goal: I can run two scripts at the same time and compare where each sprite lands.

parts.title: Higher number = ahead
parts.text: Bit (green) and Pixel (purple) both start on the green flag ▶ and run at the SAME time. On the number path, a HIGHER number means a sprite is further ahead. Read each script, find where each lands, then compare: who is ahead?

parts.title: Where does Bit land?
parts.prompt: Read Bit's script from 0: forward 4, then back 1. What number does Bit land on?

parts.title: Where does Pixel land?
parts.prompt: Read Pixel's script from 3: forward 1, then forward 1. What number does Pixel land on?

parts.title: Who is ahead?
parts.prompt: The green flag starts BOTH scripts at once. Write where each lands, then circle who is AHEAD (higher number). Bit: ____  Pixel: ____. Who is ahead, and by how many numbers?

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Both scripts run at the same time, so we can compare them. The sprite on the higher number is ahead. Here you compare Bit's landing and Pixel's landing to see who is in front.

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Students run two concurrent scripts and COMPARE the combined result: which sprite is on the higher number (ahead) and by how many. Comparing the two parallel landings — not just reading one script — is the Grade-2 C3.2 reasoning about how concurrent code behaves together.

parts.title: Ontario curriculum (Grade 2 — C3 Coding)
text: C3.1 — solve problems and create computational representations of mathematical situations by writing and executing code, including code that involves sequential and concurrent events.
C3.2 — read and alter existing code, including code that involves sequential and concurrent events, and describe how changes to the code affect the outcomes.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet and a pencil. Optional: two counters (green for Bit, purple for Pixel) on a floor number path 0-5; after 'green flag!', see whose counter ends further along.

parts.title: Run it (about 20 min)
text: 1. I DO: read Bit's script — 'start 0, forward 4 → 4, back 1 → 3.' Bit lands on 3.
2. WE DO: read Pixel's script — 'start 3, forward 1 → 4, forward 1 → 5.' Press the green flag so BOTH run together.
3. YOU DO: Exercise 3 — students compare: Pixel (5) is ahead of Bit (3) by 2 numbers.
4. Connect: 'Because both ran at the same time, we can line them up and see who is ahead.'

parts.title: Answer key (modelled by the run-gate)
text: Ex 1 — Bit: 0 → forward 4 → 4 → back 1 → 3. Bit lands on 3.
Ex 2 — Pixel: 3 → forward 1 → 4 → forward 1 → 5. Pixel lands on 5.
Ex 3 — both start on the green flag; Pixel (5) is on the higher number, so Pixel is AHEAD, by 5 − 3 = 2 numbers.
Interaction note: the two scripts run at the same time and independently — we compare their final positions to decide who is ahead.

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common error: thinking the sprite with more moves is automatically ahead — stress that 'ahead' means the higher landing NUMBER, not the longer script.
Common error: running the scripts one after the other instead of together — the green flag starts BOTH at once (concurrent).
Simplify: find each landing first, then just compare the two numbers (which is bigger?).
Extend: ask what move you could add to Bit's script so the two sprites would TIE.
Success indicator: the child lands Bit on 3 and Pixel on 5, names Pixel as ahead, and says the gap is 2.
